title: Things you do
description: Say what you eat, drink, read, and learn.
grammarNote: An -er verb in the present: como, comes, come, comemos, coméis, comen.

explanation.summary: The -er verbs follow exactly the same pattern as the -ar verbs, with two endings changed. Once you know the -ar pattern, the -er pattern is a two-minute job.

sections.heading: The six endings
sections.body: Drop the -er and add -o, -es, -e, -emos, -éis, -en. Comer becomes como, comes, come, comemos, coméis, comen. Compare with the -ar pattern: the endings are -o, -as, -a, -amos, -áis, -an. Only the second and third endings differ.

sections.heading: A spelling change to watch
sections.body: A few -er verbs change their stem in the yo form. Querer becomes quiero, poder becomes puedo, and the -er verbs with a yo ending in -go are irregular: venir becomes vengo, decir becomes digo. Learn the yo form separately from the rest.

examples.es: Leo el libro en la mesa.
examples.en: I read the book at the table.

sections.heading: Before and after
sections.body: Some verbs take a preposition, and it is fixed: hablar con, hablar de, soñar con, depender de. The preposition goes before the infinitive: hablo con Ana, sueño con la casa. The order is subject, verb, preposition, infinitive.

items.note: An infinitive ending in -er: como, comes, come.
An infinitive ending in -er: bebo, bebes, bebe.
An infinitive ending in -er: aprendo, aprendes, aprende.
An infinitive ending in -er: leo, lees, lee.
An infinitive ending in -er: vendo, vendes, vende.
An infinitive ending in -er: corro, corres, corre.
An infinitive ending in -er: pierdo, pierdes, pierde. The yo form is irregular.
An infinitive ending in -er: respondo, respondes, responde.
Feminine: la cena. Also the evening: de cena.

drills.note: Querer is irregular in the yo form.
Poder is irregular in the yo form.
